output.summary: KEP-2225 proposed building a static contributor-facing site (Hugo on Netlify) inside the kubernetes/community repo to publish and index information for upstream Kubernetes contributors. Its recorded status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Contributor documentation was spread across many repos, duplicated, out of date, and hard to find. The KEP chose a separate static site in the community repo over integrating into kubernetes.io, citing approval workflow, quality bar, and tooling concerns. The sources do not say why the KEP was marked implemented; the discussion mainly concerns when it was marked implemented and whether PRR was skipped.

alternatives.option: Do nothing and keep the markdown spread across repos
alternatives.why_not: The readme says that approach 'is not scaling and is not discoverable via Google or for other members of the contributor community.'

alternatives.option: Integrate the contributor content into the user-facing kubernetes.io site
alternatives.why_not: The readme states this is 'not preferred' because of a two-stage SIG-Docs approval workflow, a higher quality bar, and SIG-Docs already being stretched thin.

alternatives.option: Build the site in a satellite repo and import it into the main website repo
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists downsides: no pre-commit preview from Netlify, higher latency for changes, and possible presubmit failures only in the parent repo.

evidence.quote: We will build a new static site out of the [community repo](https://github.com/kubernetes/community).
The two stage approval slows down contributions and creates a much larger barrier than the current markdown based flow.
It landed after https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2672 (which made PRR required for implementable), but since it landed as implemented, it skipped PRR
Given that this KEP is related to prow, and not to anything that is contained in a kubernetes release, I think this is pretty uncontroversial
